title: [web][Android] View keeps a keyboard-reduced height and reports negative viewInsets after focus moves from an iframe input to a TextField
body:
### Steps to reproduce 1. Create a web app from the code sample below (`flutter create`, then `flutter pub add web`). It has a text input inside an iframe (`HtmlElementView`) and a Flutter `TextField`. To see where the Flutter view ends, give the page a background in `web/index.html`, for example ``. 2. `flutter build web --release`, serve `build/web`, and open it in Chrome on Android. 3. Tap the iframe input. The numeric keypad opens. 4. Tap the Flutter `TextField`. The keyboard switches to the text keyboard. 5. Close the keyboard with the system Back button or gesture. The `TextField` keeps focus. The order `TextField` → iframe input → `TextField` → Back gives the same result, which is the usual order on a form that mixes Flutter fields with an embedded payment field. ### Expected results After the keyboard closes, the Flutter view fills the viewport again and `viewInsets.bottom` is 0. ### Actual results The Flutter view stays at the height it had while the keyboard was open for the iframe input, and `viewInsets.bottom` is negative. The page background shows below the view. Measured on the page with the sample (CSS pixels; `` is its `getBoundingClientRect().height`, the last two columns are what the framework sees through `MediaQueryData.fromView`): | Step | `visualViewport.height` | `` height | view size | `viewInsets.bottom` | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Start | 692.3 | 692.3 | 384x692 | 0 | | 3. iframe input focused | 317.9 | 317.9 | 384x318 | 0 | | 4. `TextField` focused | 381.9 | 317.9 | 384x318 | -64 | | 5. Keyboard closed | 692.3 | **317.9** | **384x318** | **-374** | The view stays at 318 after tapping outside the field, and recovers the next time the keyboard opens for a Flutter text field. Same result with stable 3.47.5 and with master at 4e5a09292c. Not triggered by: - Flutter fields only (`TextField` → Back): the view stays at 692. - The iframe input only (iframe input → Back): the view follows the viewport, 318 and back to 692. #### Cause `_handleBrowserResize` keeps `_physicalSize` unchanged and reports the difference as `viewInsets` while `isMobile && textEditing.isEditing`. That relies on the preserved size being the full, keyboard-less size, the expectation #179581 describes: https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/4e5a09292c1c64a38d604c7ec096537f50d69f93/engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/window.dart#L334 https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/4e5a09292c1c64a38d604c7ec096537f50d69f93/engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/window.dart#L352-L366 That assumption does not hold when the keyboard is already open at the moment editing starts: - Step 3: the iframe input has focus, so Flutter's text editing is not active. The resize caused by the keyboard is handled as a real resize and `_physicalSize` becomes the keyboard-reduced size (318). - Step 4: the `TextField` gets focus and `isEditing` becomes true. From here `_physicalSize` is preserved at 318, and the inset is computed against it: 318 - 382 = -64 instead of 692 - 382 = 310. - Step 5: the viewport returns to 692 while the field still has focus, so the size is still preserved and the inset becomes 318 - 692 = -374. #### Where it happens - A physical Android phone (Android 16, Chrome 154.0.8037.57): the numbers and screenshots here. - An Android 14 emulator (API 34) with Chrome 113 and Chromium 157: same result. There the iframe's keypad is shorter than the text keyboard, so the inset at step 4 is positive but too small (44 instead of 274) and turns negative at step 5. - iOS is not affected. In Safari on an iOS 27 simulator the view stays at 714 through the same steps and the inset goes 0 → 330 → 0. - I first saw it with Flutter 3.44.0 on a form that has a Stripe card field (an iframe) next to Flutter text fields. #### Related - #175074 / #179581: the most recent fix in this code. It keeps the size while the keyboard is up and added the assert shown under Logs. This is a path that rule does not cover. - #173128: the same setup (an iframe input and the on-screen keyboard on Android Chrome), closed as a duplicate of #124205. - #187345: negative padding after closing the keyboard on Android Chrome, closed for lack of a reproduction. I do not know whether it has the same trigger. #### Possible fix While the size is preserved, a viewport taller than `_physicalSize` cannot be explained by a keyboard, so that resize could update `_physicalSize` instead of producing a negative inset. Patching that condition into the compiled engine of a debug build fixes the sequence above on the same phone and leaves the Flutter-only and iframe-only sequences unchanged. I can send a PR with a test in `window_test.dart` if that direction sounds right. ### Code sample
Code sample ```dart import 'dart:js_interop'; import 'dart:ui_web' as ui_web; import 'package:flutter/material.dart'; import 'package:web/web.dart' as web; void main() { // A non-Flutter text input, hosted in an iframe the way payment fields, // captchas and embedded forms are. ui_web.platformViewRegistry.registerViewFactory('iframe-input', (int id) { return web.HTMLIFrameElement() ..style.border = '0' ..style.width = '100%' ..style.height = '100%' ..srcdoc = '' .toJS; }); runApp(const App()); } class App extends StatefulWidget { const App({super.key}); @override State createState() => _AppState(); } class _AppState extends State with WidgetsBindingObserver { @override void initState() { super.initState(); WidgetsBinding.instance.addObserver(this); } @override void dispose() { WidgetsBinding.instance.removeObserver(this); super.dispose(); } // Scaffold hides the bottom inset from its body, so listen to the view // metrics directly to keep the readout current. @override void didChangeMetrics() => setState(() {}); @override Widget build(BuildContext context) { final MediaQueryData mq = MediaQueryData.fromView(View.of(context)); final String metrics = 'size=${mq.size.width.toStringAsFixed(0)}x' '${mq.size.height.toStringAsFixed(0)} ' 'insets.bottom=${mq.viewInsets.bottom.toStringAsFixed(0)}'; return MaterialApp( debugShowCheckedModeBanner: false, home: Scaffold( backgroundColor: Colors.white, body: Column( children: [ const SizedBox( height: 100, child: HtmlElementView(viewType: 'iframe-input'), ), const SizedBox( height: 80, child: Padding( padding: EdgeInsets.symmetric(horizontal: 16), child: TextField( decoration: InputDecoration(labelText: 'Flutter TextField'), ), ), ), Text(metrics), const Spacer(), Container( height: 48, width: double.infinity, color: Colors.green, alignment: Alignment.center, child: const Text('bottom of the Flutter view'), ), ], ), ), ); } } ```
### Screenshots or Video
Screenshots Steps 3, 4 and 5. The green bar marks the bottom of the Flutter view and the red area is the page background. In step 4 the gap shows above the keyboard; in step 5 the keyboard is closed.
### Logs
Logs With `flutter build web --debug`, steps 4 and 5 fail the engine's own assert in `_computeOnScreenKeyboardInsets`, before `invokeOnMetricsChanged` runs, so the framework is not told about those resizes: ```console Assertion failed: "ViewInsets cannot be negative. This is usually caused by an incorrect physicalSize calculation when the keyboard is being dismissed." at Object.wrapException (http://localhost:8765/main.dart.js:8388:47) at Object.assertThrow (http://localhost:8765/main.dart.js:8887:15) at EngineFlutterWindow._computeOnScreenKeyboardInsets$1 (http://localhost:8765/main.dart.js:70952:11) at EngineFlutterWindow._handleBrowserResize$1 (http://localhost:8765/main.dart.js:70923:15) ``` In a release build the assert is compiled out and the framework receives the negative inset shown in the table.
### Flutter Doctor output
Doctor output ```console [✓] Flutter (Channel stable, 3.47.5, on macOS 27.0.1 26A434 darwin-arm64, locale tr-TR) [508ms] • Flutter version 3.47.5 on channel stable at /Users/bilalaksoy/development/flutter • Upstream repository https://github.com/flutter/flutter.git • Framework revision 6a19cca564 (2 weeks ago), 2026-09-17 14:13:22 -0400 • Engine revision af7e796e16 • Dart version 3.13.4 • DevTools version 2.60.0 • Feature flags: enable-web, enable-linux-desktop, enable-macos-desktop, enable-windows-desktop, enable-android, enable-ios, cli-animations, enable-native-assets, enable-record-use, enable-swift-package-manager, omit-legacy-version-file, enable-lldb-debugging, enable-uiscene-migration [✓] Android toolchain - develop for Android devices (Android SDK version 36.0.0) [1.807ms] • Android SDK at /Users/bilalaksoy/Library/Android/sdk • Emulator version 37.1.11.0 (build_id 15917651) (CL:N/A) • Platform android-36, build-tools 36.0.0 • ANDROID_HOME = /Users/bilalaksoy/Library/Android/sdk • Java binary at: /Library/Java/JavaVirtualMachines/temurin-17.jdk/Contents/Home/bin/java This JDK is specified in your Flutter configuration. To change the current JDK, run: `flutter config --jdk-dir="path/to/jdk"`. • Java version OpenJDK Runtime Environment Temurin-17.0.20.1+1 (build 17.0.20.1+1) • All Android licenses accepted. [✓] Xcode - develop for iOS and macOS (Xcode 27.0) [1.080ms] • Xcode at /Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer • Build 27A266a • CocoaPods version 1.17.0 [✓] Chrome - develop for the web [6ms] • Chrome at /Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome [✓] Connected device (3 available) [6,3s] • sdk gphone64 arm64 (mobile) • emulator-5554 • android-arm64 • Android 14 (API 34) (emulator) • macOS (desktop) • macos • darwin-arm64 • macOS 27.0.1 26A434 darwin-arm64 • Chrome (web) • chrome • web-javascript • Google Chrome 153.0.8010.53 ! Error: Browsing on the local area network for iPhone. Ensure the device is unlocked and attached with a cable or associated with the same local area network as this Mac. The device must be opted into Developer Mode to connect wirelessly. (code -27) [✓] Network resources [433ms] • All expected network resources are available. • No issues found! ``` Also reproduced with master: Flutter 3.49.0-0.1.pre, framework and engine revision 4e5a09292c (2026-10-01), Dart 3.14.0-271.0.dev.
